decisions.reason: As a flagship product that sits squarely in the firm's long-standing dosimetry and calibration knowledge base and remained on the home page across 2023 and 2024, it is very likely to be retained.

The oncology risk-management software is somewhat more adjacent than core hardware QA, but it still fits the firm's software integration and workflow-improvement capabilities, so the firm is likely to keep learning and refining it rather than withdraw it.
A CT image quality phantom is closely related to the firm's established medical imaging QA competencies, making it a product the firm can readily support, interpret, and improve.
The mammography image quality phantom is strongly aligned with the firm's imaging QA business, and in a growing firm and market it is more likely to be maintained than exited.
Although its niche and possible overlap with other mammography QA offerings raise some portfolio-rationalisation risk, it still builds on the firm's existing imaging measurement and QA expertise.

This imaging QA instrument line was presented as a strategic focus and draws directly on the firm's core scientific, engineering, calibration, and service capabilities, so withdrawal within a year is unlikely.
